title: The blunt-to-sharp join comparison is a categorical equivalence
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and functor equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $X,Y$ be arbitrary small simplicial sets in the fixed universe. Define the sharp join by
$$(X\star Y)_n=X_n\amalg Y_n\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=n}X_a\times Y_b,$$
where $a,b\geq0$ and the operators restrict the ordered block of $X$-vertices followed by the ordered block of $Y$-vertices; an empty block is represented by the corresponding pure $X$- or $Y$-simplex. Define $X\diamond Y$ degreewise as the quotient of $X\amalg(X\times\Delta^1\times Y)\amalg Y$ identifying $(x,0,y)$ with $x$ and $(x,1,y)$ with $y$, with induced simplicial operators. On an $n$-simplex $(x,t,y)$ of the cylinder, where $t:[n]\to[1]$, restrict $x$ to the initial block $t^{-1}(0)$ and $y$ to the final block $t^{-1}(1)$ and concatenate them. Together with the inclusions on the pure summands, this defines the comparison $c_{X,Y}:X\diamond Y\to X\star Y$, which is the identity on the two distinguished copies of $X$ and $Y$.
For every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a sufficiently large universe, precomposition induces a functor equivalence
$$c_{X,Y}^{*}:\operatorname{Fun}(X\star Y,\mathcal E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(X\diamond Y,\mathcal E).$$
Here functor equivalence has the quasi-inverse and coherent natural equivalence meaning of the cited definition. No quasicategory, nonemptiness or finiteness assumption is imposed on $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Example 4.6.4.9, functor-category formulation of the blunt-to-sharp categorical equivalence (Theorem 4.6.2.8); the comparison is defined in Notation 4.6.2.3. Read the example and both referenced statements online 2026-10-17. Kerodon, not the Stacks Project; not archived under literature/.

proof.text:
For a degree $r$, let $T_r$ be the set of nonconstant weakly increasing maps $[r]\to[1]$; in particular $T_0=\varnothing$. The defining quotient has the disjoint normal form
$$(X\diamond Y)_r=X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg(X_r\times T_r\times Y_r).$$
Indeed, a cylinder simplex with constant interval coordinate is identified with exactly its indicated pure endpoint simplex; no relation involves a nonconstant interval coordinate, nor identifies distinct pure simplices. Operators on these classes restrict the cylinder coordinates and collapse to the indicated pure summand when the interval becomes constant. The formula for $c_{X,Y}$ is well-defined on the quotient: for a constant interval it is the corresponding pure inclusion. Restricting along $\alpha:[s]\to[r]$ restricts the zero and one blocks to their inverse images under $\alpha$, so either route gives the same concatenation, also when a block becomes empty. Maps in $X$ and $Y$ commute with these restrictions. Consequently $\diamond$, $\star$ are ordinary bifunctors and $c$ is a natural transformation in both variables, fixing both pure summands.

source.place: Notation 4.6.2.3 (01HR): degreewise quotient, comparison and its naturality; explicit argument supplied here, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Both bifunctors preserve degreewise injections and all small connected colimits separately in each variable. For fixed $Y$, the displayed normal form is a constant summand $Y_r$ plus $X_r\times(\{*\}\amalg(T_r\times Y_r))$, while the sharp-join formula is $Y_r\amalg X_r\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=r}(X_a\times Y_b)$. In a nonempty connected indexing category, the colimit of the constant summand is one copy of that summand: arrows identify its copies, connectedness identifies any two copies, and no arrow changes its value. The other summands commute with colimits of sets: their generating relations change only the variable simplex, leaving the summand label and the fixed coordinate unchanged. Thus a class is precisely a class of variable simplices with the fixed label and coordinate. These bijections commute with all simplicial operators. For fixed $X$, the blunt-join normal form is $X_r\amalg(Y_r\times(\{*\}\amalg(X_r\times T_r)))$, and the sharp-join formula is $X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{a+b+1=r}(X_a\times Y_b)$. For a connected diagram in $Y$, the constant $X_r$ copies are identified to one copy, and every other generating relation changes only the $Y$ coordinate, preserving the fixed $X$ coordinate and the summand label. Its quotient classes are therefore precisely the corresponding $Y$-colimit classes with those labels. Restriction of simplices preserves these descriptions, giving the canonical simplicial colimit isomorphisms in this variable as well. The formulas also show directly that injections stay injective. Degreewise set colimits give simplicial-set colimits: define operators on representatives, and their universal property is the compatible family of set universal properties. Finally, $\varnothing\diamond Y=\varnothing\star Y=Y$ and $X\diamond\varnothing=X\star\varnothing=X$, with $c$ the identity in either case.

source.place: Theorem 4.6.2.8 (01HV): preservation hypotheses for a two-variable cellular reduction; explicit argument supplied here, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Take $X=\Delta^m$, $Y=\Delta^n$, with $m,n\geq0$, and put $P=X\diamond Y$, $Q=X\star Y=\Delta^{m+n+1}$. The last equality identifies a mixed simplex with its weakly increasing list of initial vertices in $[m]$ followed by vertices in $[n]$, shifted by $m+1$; the pure lists supply the remaining cases. The cylinder is the nerve of the product poset $D=[m]\times[1]\times[n]$, since a chain in the product is a triple of chains. Define a monotone map $f:D\to[m+n+1]$ by $f(a,0,b)=a$ and $f(a,1,b)=m+1+b$. Its induced nerve map descends through the endpoint quotient to exactly $c:P\to Q$. The monotone map $k:[m+n+1]\to D$ given by $k(a)=(a,0,0)$ for $a\leq m$ and $k(m+1+b)=(m,1,b)$ gives $s:Q\to P$ by the quotient map. Crossing from the first block to the second is monotone because $a\leq m$ and $0\leq b$. The equality $fk=1$ gives $cs=1_Q$. These constructions include $m=0$ and $n=0$.

source.place: Theorem 4.6.2.8 (01HV), simplex-pair case: explicit section of the comparison; explicit argument supplied here, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: On $D$ define $g(a,0,b)=(a,0,0)$, $g(a,1,b)=(a,1,b)$, and $h=kf$, so $h(a,0,b)=(a,0,0)$ and $h(a,1,b)=(m,1,b)$. They are monotone: within either layer each coordinate is nondecreasing, and crossing layers gives $(a,0,0)\leq(a',1,b')$ for $g$ and $(a,0,0)\leq(m,1,b')$ for $h$. Pointwise $g\leq1_D$ and $g\leq h$. Each inequality $u\leq v$ gives the monotone map $D\times[1]\to D$ with values $u$ and $v$ on the two layers: for $d\leq d'$ the crossing inequality is $u(d)\leq u(d')\leq v(d')$. Its nerve is a simplicial homotopy. The two homotopies descend to $P\times\Delta^1$: on the bottom layer the quotient always retains just $a$, and on the top layer it always retains just $b$, independent of the homotopy parameter. Products with the parameter preserve the quotient, since its generating relations never change that coordinate. Thus there is a self-map $\bar g:P\to P$ and homotopies $\bar g\Rightarrow1_P$, $\bar g\Rightarrow sc$. Each is the constant homotopy on the entire pure copies of $X$ and $Y$, so its edge at every vertex of $P$ is degenerate.

source.place: Theorem 4.6.2.8 (01HV), simplex-pair case: explicit zigzag of homotopies relative to the pure summands; explicit argument supplied here, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal E)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\mathcal E)$, quasicategories by [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory]. The maps $c,s$ give $c^*:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ and $s^*:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ with $s^*c^*=1$. Let $V\subseteq P$ consist of the constant simplices at vertices, and put $B=P\times\mathcal A$, $A_0=V\times\mathcal A$. Evaluate the two homotopies of Step 4 to obtain a map $B\times\Lambda_0^2\to\mathcal E$, using $\bar g\Rightarrow1_P$ on $01$ and $\bar g\Rightarrow sc$ on $02$. Explicitly, a simplex $F:P\times\Delta^r\to\mathcal E$ is sent to $(x,t,z)\mapsto F(H(x,t),z)$, which commutes with restriction of every coordinate. On $A_0$ both homotopies are constant in $t$; extend there to $A_0\times\Delta^2$ by evaluation ignoring the triangle coordinate. These prescriptions agree on the overlap. At every vertex $(x,F)$ of $B$, edge $01$ is degenerate. Thus [lem-cbc-invertible-prism-extension] applies to $A_0\subseteq B$, $n=2$, $Q=\mathcal E$. Curry edge $12$ of its filler to obtain a coherent transformation $\eta:1_{\mathcal A}\Rightarrow c^*s^*$. Its evaluation at every vertex $x$ of $P$ is degenerate, since the filler has the prescribed restriction on $A_0$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] with $K=P$, each $\eta_F$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal A$; by the same statement with $K=\mathcal A$, $\eta$ is an equivalence edge in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal A,\mathcal A)$. Enlarge the universe for these products and functor objects. Together with $s^*c^*=1$ this makes $s^*$ a coherent quasi-inverse to $c^*$, in exactly the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This proves the simplex-pair case.

source.place: Theorem 4.6.2.8 (01HV) and Example 4.6.4.9 (05YH): explicit functor quasi-inverse in the simplex-pair case; explicit argument supplied here, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: For each fixed $m\geq0$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-cellular-natural-equivalence] to the functors $P_m(Y)=\Delta^m\diamond Y$ and $Q_m(Y)=\Delta^m\star Y$ with natural transformation $c_{\Delta^m,Y}$. Step 2 proves preservation of injections and all small connected colimits, and identifies $c_{\Delta^m,\varnothing}$ as the identity. Step 5 proves the simplex hypotheses for every $\Delta^n$, with the full functor-equivalence convention required by the cited criterion. Consequently, for every small $Y$ and every quasicategory $\mathcal E$ in a sufficiently large universe, $c_{\Delta^m,Y}^*$ is a functor equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 4.6.2.8 (01HV): first cellular extension, in the second variable; explicit argument supplied here, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Now fix any small $Y$ and apply [lem-coef-infinity-cellular-natural-equivalence] to $P^Y(X)=X\diamond Y$ and $Q^Y(X)=X\star Y$ and their natural comparison. Step 2 verifies the preservation hypotheses and the identity $c_{\varnothing,Y}$; Step 6 verifies every standard-simplex hypothesis. The criterion therefore gives, for every small $X$, exactly the required functor equivalence $c_{X,Y}^*$. No finiteness, quasicategory or nonemptiness condition on either factor entered the argument. In particular if a factor is empty the comparison was already the identity in Step 2.

source.place: Theorem 4.6.2.8 (01HV): second cellular extension, in the first variable; explicit argument supplied here, not archived under literature/.

proof_origin.place: Explicit simplex-pair section and two relative homotopies, extended separately in each variable using the existing cellular criterion. Kerodon Theorem 4.6.2.8 (01HV) and Example 4.6.4.9 (05YH) give the conclusion; this is an agent-written proof, not their published reduction to Delta^1. Online sources read 2026-10-17, not archived.
